description: A crypto investor has significant capital gains from one asset but losses in others. They need to execute 'tax-loss harvesting' before the year-end, but face 'wash-sale' rule conflicts. They need a plan to minimize tax liability without violating regulations.

fact_sheet.fact: The investor's name is Alex Chen, and he is a 28-year-old Senior Software Engineer at Innovatech Solutions.
Alex Chen's projected annual taxable income for the 2023 tax year is $185,000.
Alex Chen sold 500 units of the cryptocurrency Solara (SOLA) on December 15, 2023, realizing a long-term capital gain of $150,000.
The cost basis for the 500 SOLA units was $25,000, purchased on January 10, 2023, at $50 per unit.
Alex holds 2,000 units of Etherium Classic Fork (ECF), which he purchased on May 5, 2023.
The total cost basis for the 2,000 ECF units is $80,000, with an average purchase price of $40 per unit.
As of December 16, 2023, the 2,000 ECF units have a market value of $20,000, representing an unrealized short-term loss of $60,000.
Alex also holds 10,000 units of QuantumLeap (QTM), which he purchased on October 2, 2023.
The total cost basis for the 10,000 QTM units is $30,000, with an average purchase price of $3 per unit.
As of December 16, 2023, the 10,000 QTM units have a market value of $5,000, representing an unrealized short-term loss of $25,000.
The applicable federal long-term capital gains tax rate for Alex's income bracket is 15%.
Without any loss harvesting, Alex's estimated federal tax liability on the SOLA gain is $22,500.
The plan is to sell all 2,000 ECF units and all 10,000 QTM units on December 28, 2023.
This sale will realize a combined short-term capital loss of $85,000 ($60,000 from ECF and $25,000 from QTM).
The $85,000 in realized losses will be used to offset the $150,000 SOLA gain, reducing the net taxable capital gain to $65,000.
After executing the plan, the new estimated federal tax liability will be $9,750, resulting in a tax savings of $12,750.
The wash-sale rule, as interpreted by IRS Notice 2014-21 for crypto, disallows a loss deduction if a substantially identical asset is purchased within 30 days before or after the sale.
To maintain market exposure without triggering the wash-sale rule, Alex plans to buy a non-identical asset, ChainLink Alternative (CLX), with the proceeds from the ECF and QTM sales.
Alex cannot repurchase ECF or QTM until at least January 28, 2024, to comply with the 30-day wash-sale window.
All of Alex's crypto transactions are executed on the Zenith Digital Asset Exchange (ZDAX).
Alex's user ID for the Zenith Digital Asset Exchange is 'AChen_88'.
Alex uses the premium version of the CoinStats app to track his portfolio's real-time value and cost basis.
He will use the Koinly tax software to generate IRS Form 8949 by importing his ZDAX transaction CSV file.
Alex consulted with a tax professional, Chloe Davis, from the firm 'FinOptima Advisory' to create this plan.
The consultation with Chloe Davis took place via a 45-minute Zoom call on December 12, 2023.
Chloe Davis's professional recommendation was to document the rationale for CLX not being 'substantially identical' to ECF in case of an audit.
